key_insight: The paper benchmarks four operator-learning deep models for aerodynamics and finds that Bi-Stride Multi-Scale Graph Neural Network and Transolver(++) are the most promising for surrogate prediction of pressure fields.
engineering_relevance: These surrogate models can reduce the cost of CFD by rapidly predicting airfoil and aircraft pressure distributions for design optimization, load analysis, and other simulation-heavy aerospace tasks.
method: Tested two scenarios: 2D airfoils with varying complexity and an industrial-scale 3D aircraft configuration.
Evaluated shock capture, scalability to large meshes, and performance under limited data.
evidence_signal: The benchmark uses two experiments on aerodynamic pressure prediction across 2D and 3D geometries, specifically assessing discontinuities, mesh-scale handling, and data scarcity.
watch_item: Performance may vary significantly by geometry and data regime, so deployment should verify robustness on the target aerodynamic configuration before replacing high-fidelity solvers.
paper_title: Evaluation of State-of-the-Art Deep Learning Architectures for Aerodynamical Predictions
